STEP 1 - Scene: A small green salad (mixed arugula/rocket-style leaves with a few dark olives or berries and thin red pepper or carrot strips), photographed from above on a white square plate.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate, roughly 26 cm across on its longest side. Plate area approx. 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2 (treating it as a circle-equivalent; square plate about 600 cm^2 at corners). Use ~550 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: mixed leafy greens (arugula/rocket and some lettuce), 3-4 dark olives, a few thin red pepper strips. No visible dressing pool, only a light sheen at most.

STEP 4 - Area: Leaves cover roughly 25% of the plate (the salad spans the central-right area, not the full plate). Olives ~1%. Red strips ~1%. Total food coverage about 27%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Leaves: 25% of 550 = 138 cm^2 x 3 cm loose pile = ~410 ml. Olives: about 4 olives, ~2 cm^3 each = ~8 ml, and red pepper ~3 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Leaves 410 ml x 0.15 = ~62 g. Olives 8 ml x 0.9 = ~7 g. Pepper 3 ml x 0.6 = ~2 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Leafy greens ~25 kcal/100 g: 62 g → ~15 kcal. Olives ~115 kcal/100 g: 7 g → ~8 kcal. Red pepper ~30 kcal/100 g: 2 g → <1 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A light side salad of about 70 g with roughly 25 kcal is plausible for what is visible, and it is well under the several hundred grams a fully covered dinner plate would hold. Total ≈ 71 g, ≈ 24 kcal.
